title: Quality and appropriateness of the researcher's professional experience, competences and skills
content:
## 1.4 Quality and appropriateness of the researcher's professional experience, competences and skills

### 1.4.1 An experienced researcher whose profile is matched to a training-through-research action

FIELDWISE is carried out by the experienced researcher Dr. Rositsa Cholakova, who holds a doctorate and therefore meets the MSCA-PF experienced-researcher condition. Her professional experience is appropriate to this fellowship in a specific and demanding sense: MSCA-PF is a training-through-research action, so the relevant test is not that the researcher already possesses every competence the project requires, but that her existing experience is strong exactly where the project's scientific object is anchored, is genuinely complementary to what the host adds, and defines a coherent development trajectory. On all three counts her profile fits the action. Her established strength is the biological, physiological and agronomic half of the project — precisely the half that the host's remote-sensing and geoinformatics groups do not themselves hold — while the geospatial, uncertainty-aware modelling half is the deliberate, structured gap the fellowship is designed to close (see §1.3). Her professional experience is therefore not merely adequate but load-bearing for the interdisciplinary integration that §1.2 identifies as constitutive of the objectives O1–O6.

### 1.4.2 Depth in the project's core discipline: plant physiology, agronomy and the model crop

The scientific core of FIELDWISE — a physiologically meaningful definition of crop water stress in processing tomato, observed through soil, meteorological and hyperspectral data — sits squarely within Dr. Cholakova's trained expertise. She completed her PhD in Plant Physiology at Agricultural University – Plovdiv (doctoral studies 2014–2020, EQF level 8), with doctoral research in plant stress physiology (her thesis, an English rendering of the Bulgarian original, concerns the response of maize to low temperatures and the effectiveness of subsequent foliar fertilisation), supervised by Prof. Dr. Andon Vassilev. She has since held the post of Assistant Professor in Plant Physiology and Plant Stress Physiology at the same university (2015–2020) and is currently Chief Assistant Professor and plant physiology researcher at the Maritsa Vegetable Crops Research Institute (from 15 October 2024). This is the disciplinary competence — plant physiology, horticultural crop science, plant protection/agronomy, water-stress experimentation, physiological phenotyping and hyperspectral field measurement — that she transfers to the host under the fellow→host direction of knowledge transfer, and it is what makes WP1 (Historical Data and Target Design) and WP2 (Physiological Early Warning and Hyperspectral-to-Sentinel Transfer) achievable: only a plant physiologist can define the physiological stress target the geospatial model must learn to predict.

Her current research directly concerns the FIELDWISE crop and the FIELDWISE stress. She works on project ZEMDKT 17 (2024–2026), whose Task 7 studies resistance to abiotic stress — drought and salinity — in Solanum lycopersicum, i.e. tomato under water and osmotic stress, and she participates in SolGenSys (2026–2030) on tomato multi-stress tolerance. Her experience is thus not adjacent to the project's biology; it is the same crop and the same physiological problem the fellowship addresses, which is the strongest available evidence that the researcher can execute the physiological programme rather than merely commission it.

### 1.4.3 An emerging, honestly-scoped Earth-observation and geospatial track record

The appropriateness argument is stated with candour rather than overstatement. The Earth-observation and geospatial side of Dr. Cholakova's profile is emerging, not yet consolidated: of her body of published work, only three items touch remote sensing, all dated 2025 or later and all with her as a middle author, so the EO half of her profile rests not on a publication record but on demonstrable, hands-on engagement with geospatial method — namely a COST Action CA22136 (PANGEOS) Short-Term Scientific Mission hosted at MATE in Hungary in 2025; three Erasmus+ staff-mobility grants to MATE (Hungary) and the University of Novi Sad (Serbia) in 2025–2026; an Erasmus PhD mobility to the Timiryazev Academy in Moscow (2018); and an operational A1/A3 UAV pilot licence issued by the Civil Aviation Administration of Bulgaria. She is a member of three COST Actions (CA22136 PANGEOS, CA22149 AI4Insect and CA22141 REcrop) and participates in KP-06-COST/2 (2025–ongoing), which monitors vegetable crops for precision agriculture using satellite and unmanned aerial systems together with the Space Research and Technology Institute of the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences. She has also begun the transition formally, undertaking a second MSc in Environmental Engineering (2025–2026), and has already built preliminary technical capacity by initiating the DrR - Digital Agronomist prototype that integrates soil-sensor, field-meteorological and Sentinel-2 data. Presenting this evidence as a credible but incomplete geospatial foundation — rather than claiming a finished EO scientist's CV — is what makes the fellowship's training rationale honest: there is a real gap in Bayesian/probabilistic modelling, spatio-temporal AI, sensor-domain transfer, uncertainty quantification, cross-country adaptation and decision evaluation, and FIELDWISE is designed to close it.

### 1.4.4 Transferable competences: teaching, inter-sectoral exposure and proposal maturity

Beyond the two scientific halves, the researcher brings transferable competences that materially strengthen the action. She has five years of university teaching at Agricultural University – Plovdiv (2015–2020), including syllabus design, lecturing and examining in both Bulgarian and English (including for Erasmus students) and the supervision of Bachelor's theses, together with specialist advisory work for farmers on physiological monitoring and integrated plant protection. This is why the fellowship's teaching component (§1.3) is framed as an existing strength transferred to a new discipline, a new institution and a new language of instruction, rather than a competence to be acquired — a direct contribution to the call's expected outcome on feeding research results back into teaching (EO-08). She additionally holds recent non-academic experience as a Data Analyst at KPMG Global Hungary (2024) and earlier as an agricultural market analyst, giving her prior exposure both to data-analytic practice and to a commercial working environment — relevant preparation for the operational, decision-value and non-academic-placement components of WP5 (Operational Transfer, Decision Value and Web MVP). Finally, the researcher has already carried a closely related concept through the full MSCA-PF process: the predecessor application PLANTDIGISENSE (HORIZON-MSCA-2025-PF, proposal 101284764), with the same host, scored 70.40% against a 70.00 threshold, demonstrating that she can design and articulate a fundable research programme at this level. FIELDWISE is a strengthened resubmission by a researcher who has already reached the threshold, not an untested first attempt.

### 1.4.5 Prior familiarity with the host environment and the intended career trajectory

Dr. Cholakova's experience is also appropriate to this particular host and this particular mobility. Her documented mobilities have repeatedly brought her into the Hungarian research environment and, specifically, into contact with the host and its partners — a PANGEOS STSM and Erasmus+ staff mobilities at MATE, an Erasmus master's mobility internship at ELTE in 2026, and a period of professional activity in Budapest — so she arrives already familiar with the host country, the partner MATE that supplies the source-domain dataset, and the host institution itself. This lowers the integration risk of the fellowship and reinforces the two-way transfer described in §1.3. Her experience maps onto a clear and realistic career progression: from Plant Physiologist/Agronomist, through EO/Geospatial Crop Scientist, to an independent researcher in transferable agricultural intelligence. The fellowship supplies exactly the missing segment of that trajectory — advanced competence in Bayesian/probabilistic modelling, uncertainty quantification, spatio-temporal validation, sensor-domain transfer, cross-country adaptation, operational AI evaluation and research-to-MVP translation — and the experience she already holds is what makes that acquisition credible within 30 months. In accordance with the call, her intervening career break (full-time parenting, July 2021–May 2024) is declared in Part A and does not count against the experienced-researcher time ceiling, so it does not diminish the appropriateness of her research experience. The result is a researcher whose existing professional experience is deep where the science is anchored, honestly emerging where the fellowship trains, and directly aligned with the call's expected outcomes on increased research and transferable skills and improved employability (EO-01) and on new inter-sectoral, interdisciplinary mind-sets (EO-02). Note on identity: the researcher publishes her pre-2020 work under the name Rositsa Cholakova-Bimbalova and her later work under Rositsa Cholakova; both name forms denote the same person and both are carried in Part A so that the full record attaches to the applicant.

claim_statuses.claim_summary: The fellow is the experienced researcher Dr. Rositsa Cholakova (PhD-holder), the applicant for this MSCA-PF action.
She holds a PhD in Plant Physiology from Agricultural University – Plovdiv (doctoral studies 2014–2020, EQF 8), supervised by Prof. Dr. Andon Vassilev.
Her doctoral research concerned the response of maize to low temperatures and the effectiveness of subsequent foliar fertilisation (plant stress physiology).
Pre-2020 work is published as Rositsa Cholakova-Bimbalova and later work as Rositsa Cholakova; both denote the same applicant and both are carried in Part A.

She is Chief Assistant Professor and plant physiology researcher at the Maritsa Vegetable Crops Research Institute from 15 October 2024, and was previously Assistant Professor in Plant (Stress) Physiology at AU Plovdiv 2015–2020.

Her established competences are plant physiology, horticultural crop science, plant protection/agronomy, water-stress experimentation, physiological phenotyping and hyperspectral field measurement (fellow→host transfer).
She works on ZEMDKT 17 (2024–2026, drought/salinity in Solanum lycopersicum) and SolGenSys (2026–2030, tomato multi-stress tolerance) — the same crop and stress as FIELDWISE.

Only three of her publications touch remote sensing (2025+, middle author), so the EO half of her profile rests on the PANGEOS STSM at MATE (2025), Erasmus+ mobilities, an Erasmus PhD mobility (2018) and a UAV pilot licence rather than on publications.

She is a member of COST Actions CA22136 PANGEOS, CA22149 AI4Insect and CA22141 REcrop, participates in KP-06-COST/2 satellite/UAV monitoring with SRTI-BAS, and holds an A1/A3 UAV pilot licence from the Civil Aviation Administration of Bulgaria.
She is undertaking a second MSc in Environmental Engineering (AU Plovdiv, 2025–2026).
She has undertaken preliminary development of the DrR - Digital Agronomist prototype integrating soil-sensor, field-meteorological and Sentinel-2 data.

She has five years of university teaching at AU Plovdiv (2015–2020) — syllabus design, lecturing and examining in Bulgarian and English including for Erasmus students, and Bachelor's thesis supervision — framed as an existing strength.
She has recent non-academic experience as a Data Analyst at KPMG Global Hungary (2024) and earlier as an agricultural market analyst.
The predecessor application PLANTDIGISENSE (HORIZON-MSCA-2025-PF, proposal 101284764) at the same host scored 70.40% against a 70.00 threshold; FIELDWISE is a strengthened resubmission.

The fellowship addresses her competence gap (Bayesian/probabilistic modelling, spatio-temporal AI, sensor-domain transfer, uncertainty, cross-country adaptation, decision evaluation) along the progression Plant Physiologist/Agronomist → EO/Geospatial Crop Scientist → independent researcher in transferable agricultural intelligence.

Her mobilities (PANGEOS STSM and Erasmus+ at MATE, an Erasmus master's internship at ELTE in 2026, and prior activity in Budapest) mean she arrives already familiar with the host country, MATE and the host institution.
Her career break (full-time parenting, July 2021–May 2024) is declared in Part A and does not count against the experienced-researcher time ceiling.
The host beneficiary is Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE), whose remote-sensing/geoinformatics competence complements the fellow's plant-science profile.
The action is a European Fellowship (with a six-month non-academic placement extension), a training-through-research action.
The action runs 30 months, within which the researcher's development trajectory is realised.

The researcher's experience and development align with call expected outcomes EO-01 (increased research/transferable skills, employability), EO-02 (new inter-sectoral/interdisciplinary mind-sets) and EO-08 (research results feeding into teaching).

Whether the European Fellowship mobility rule is satisfied rests on an operator-declared assumption (rectified CV giving 7.05 months in Hungary against a 12-month cap); the CV's face count is contested and it is not confirmed.
